To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the correlation between the classification of microcalcification according to the BI-RADS lexicon and the underlying histologic diagnosis is statistically significant.

the correlation between the BI-RADS assessment categories 3 (benign), 4 (probably benign), and 5 (suspicious for malignancy) and the underlying histological findings is highly significant (P < 0.0001), and that the sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value increase with increasing BI-RADS category.

microcalcifications of breast lesions are classified according to the morphology and distribution pattern as described in the BI-RADS lexicon and that the classification correlates with the histology.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and implementation of a new classification system for microcalcifications of breast lesions, which is intended to facilitate communication between radiologists and surgeons, as well as to improve the quality of the radiological diagnosis.
a more precise classification of microcalcification findings in mammography.
the question of whether and to what degree the pre-biopsic classification of microcalcification patterns is correlated with the histologic findings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a BI-RADS® classification 3/4 or 5 is not an absolute indication for biopsy, but a high suspicion for malignancy.
a microcalcification with BI-RADS® category 3 is not malignant, whereas BI-RADS® assessments 4 and 5 are highly suggestive for malignancy.
the BI-RADS classification of microcalcification is a useful diagnostic tool in the clinical routine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BI-RADS classification system of microcalcifications of mammography is a valuable tool to predict the probability of malignancy of a lesion and to guide the decision for biopsy.
the radiological assessment of microcalcifications in the breast is an important tool for the detection of malignancy.
a BI-RADS® category 5 assessment is highly predictive of malignancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radiologists should not be afraid of classifying microcalcifications in the BI-RADS categories.
the BI-RADS classification of microcalcification is not a reliable predictor for underlying malignancy.

the radiological assessment of breast microcalcifications is an important diagnostic tool in breast imaging and should be considered as a part of the clinical workup of a patient with a suspicious mammographic finding.
